findings.issue: Each checked int128 multiplication is printed as four sign-case comparisons and each checked add/sub as two, all repeating the full operand expressions over the Point struct kept in memory (mem[_2], mem[_2 + 32] ...), so one source line of _checkpoint becomes 6-8 lines; the bound of 'MULTIPLIER * x' prints as the hex quotient of 2^256-1 by 1e18.
findings.rule: Recognise the four-case signed-overflow test of a * b (and the two-case test of a + b) as one 'checked signed mul/add' (like SafeMath.mul for unsigned), bind its operands once, keep the memory struct fields as named locals (P14), and print a constant equal to floor((2^256-1)/10**k) as that quotient.

notes: Reviewed against ve.sol (the Solidly/Curve-style voting escrow). The functions are all under 510 lines and were read by structure: nonreentrant, _isApprovedOrOwner checks, _checkpoint's 255-week loop (inlined in 10 functions), the binary searches, deposit/withdraw token transfers, merge, ERC-721 transfers with onERC721Received, tokenURI's SVG building with toString and Base64. Loops: 8 source loops (the Base64 Yul for, _find_block_epoch's and balanceOfAtNFT's 128-step binary searches, the totalSupplyAt search, _checkpoint's 255 loop, _supply_at's 255 loop, toString's two while loops) all shown as while in every inlined copy; implicit: the string concatenations and copies of tokenURI (P7, about 24 whiles). P4: user_point_history / slope_changes keys read from memory words. No P2 and only one hidden revert. No execution run.
summary: Faithful with all 8 loops present and no P2; the checkpoint arithmetic on int128 is buried under four-case signed-overflow checks repeated for every operation, with the Point struct kept in memory.
